question: Who among the following said, "The Rowlatt Act is a preventive murder"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Edwin Samuel Montagu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Edwin Samuel Montagu** was a British Liberal politician.
 
• He served as the Secretary of State for India from 1917 to 1922.
 
• Montagu was known for his progressive views on Indian self-governance and played a significant role in the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
 
• He famously criticized the Rowlatt Act, referring to it as "preventive murder".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rowlatt Act**

 
 
• The Rowlatt Act, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, was a legislative act passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in British India.
 
• It gave the colonial government enormous powers to suppress subversive activities and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years.
 
• This act was widely opposed by Indian leaders, leading to a nationwide protest known as the Rowlatt Satyagraha led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The act was eventually repealed in 1922 due to widespread public outrage and opposition.
 
 
 
• **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**
 
 
• The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were introduced by Edwin Montagu and Lord Chelmsford in 1919.
 
• The reforms aimed to introduce self-governing institutions gradually to India.
 
• They led to the Government of India Act 1919, which expanded the participation of Indians in the governance of their country.
 
• The reforms also introduced a dual system of governance known as 'dyarchy' in the provinces.
